answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable deposit in a shared vault before it can trade: the deposit is tied to one verified hardware key, like a ferrous token sealed in a device, so one machine cannot mint many personas. A newcomer earns a haven of trust only after its deposit ages without misbehavior. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of locked deposits plus hardware, while honest agents pay nothing beyond temporary illiquidity.
